Children playing with worthless Deutsche Mark currency. Germany. c. 1923

The hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic was a three-year period between June 1921 and January 1924. In 1918, German marks traded at 7.9 marks per American dollar. During the first half of 1922, the mark stabilized at about 320 Marks per dollar but by November of 1923, the dollar was worth 4,210,500,000,000 German marks.

In order to pay for the costs of the World War One, Germany suspended the gold standard (i.e., the convertibility of its currency into gold) when the war broke out. The German Emperor Wilhelm II and the German parliament (the Reichstag) decided without opposition to fund the war entirely by borrowing as it believed that it would be able to pay off the debt by annexing resource-rich industrial territory to the west and east and imposing massive reparations on the defeated Allies. That strategy obviously backfired when Germany lost the war. The new Weimar Republic was now saddled with a massive war debt that it could not afford, made even worse by the fact that it was printing money without the economic resources to back it up.

Beginning in August 1921, Germany began to buy foreign currency with marks at any price, but that only increased the speed of breakdown in the value of the mark. The lower the mark sank in international markets, the greater the amount of marks was required to buy the foreign currency demanded by the Reparations Commission.

Am I a patriot? Depends on the definition of the term. Andrew Jackson once said,

Americans are not a perfect people, but we are called to a perfect mission.

I don't think of America as a place or a people, I think of it as a mission, an ideal to strive for. That's what American Exceptionalism means to me. It means unlike other countries we were not founded to compete with other nations in the same old game of thrones. We were founded to change the game, to spearhead the evolution of human society into policy based on rationality and utility rather than instinct and tradition. As long as I keep faith in that mission, I am a patriot.

I am not a Patriot, in any way that word can be interpreted. Also, I happen to have a mildly negative outlook on everyone who describes themselves a Patriot.

See, I am a traveler. I have spent significant amounts of time in multiple countries, and I have met people and made friends with people from even more countries. Everyone is flawed, everyone is beautiful, everyone has their own rich set of culture, jokes, traditions, food. Everyone believes in different things, most ideals are incompatible. Most people believe they are from the best country from the planet, and many of these people are patriotic to their own countries. I love many of these countries, I hate some of them and I don't care about some others.

Patriotism starts loosing value when you find one other country where you can be just as happy living in. Often, you'll find at least 3 different countries where you wouldn't mind living.

I am also a fan of History. I have a deep bias against any person of authority who finds himself/herself in a situation where they end up calling for "patriots" to "serve" their country. While the patriots are genuinely people who love the country, there has been zero examples in history so far where the person calling upon them to serve has been honest about what they were fighting for and what the patriots were dying for.

One must only ask the question of why patriotism is encouraged as a good thing to start going down strange dark roads into human nature. Is there truly one good country in the world surrounded on all sides by horrible monsters? The answer is obviously a no! Then why does the concept of being patriotic to one country even exist? More interestingly, why is it so commonly found among such large groups of people? Who planted ideas into a population, and who is working to sustain the idea of patriotism? As Cicero would say, "Cui bono"?

We live in a world where young boys are a victim to brainwashing by very powerful government agencies with an endless appetite of disposable meat in their armies. From paying NFL to have players salute soldiers during Superbowl to having misleading speeches in Sea World shows to unreal advertisements about Military service to encouraging movies and video games that makes soldiers appear cool - We have built a society that really encourages people to go serve.

One of the most depressing moment in my life was when I was staying at a hotel in San Jose. I ran into an 18 y.o kid in the elevator. Asked him what he was doing - it was one day before his start of service in the military. He was super thrilled. He told me how excited he was to be able to go out and be a bad-ass. That boy had no idea that he had just been reduced to a number, a statistic, a resource and a weapon, to be used by the kind of people that he would grow to hate and then forgotten by the country when he was older, had PTSD and would face a long life of terrible V.A lines and unfulfilled promises.

To me, the idea of "Patriotism" is more than a simple love for a country. It is a tool - a bait for a trap designed to capture young teenagers who don't understand the world - and then sent straight into a meat grinder at the smallest opportunity.

So no, I am not a Patriot. I would be if there was a country that was truly worth fighting for - one worth dying for. But the only place such a country can exist is in my head - the real world is built in a way that only the ambitious and ruthless power hungry ass holes reach positions of authority that can call upon patriots.

Not really. I support the things that America stands for in theory (liberty, free speech, etc) but I don't believe the country is inherently exceptional nor do I support what it has turned in to. I don't believe in concepts like the draft (IMO it is nothing other than slavery) but I am not opposed to military service in itself
